text:
Alex Cohen: Quick heads-up from the night perf run — continuous-batching memory accounting is underestimating per-sequence overhead (KV + transient workspace) for short sequences. Caused a cascade where batch size grows beyond safe bounds and we get intermittent OOMs on dedicated GPU pools.

Alex Cohen: Repro on staging: saw ~6 OOMs across 60k requests when seq_len distribution skewed to 8-16 tokens. Profiler shows batch estimator uses 'effective_seq' = max(seq_lengths) but misses per-seq kv headers. Log excerpt: 
```
[2026-02-25 03:12:11] batch_estimator: target_slots=48; sum_seq=320; effective_seq=16; predicted_bytes=1.2GB; actual_resident=1.45GB; oom_after_alloc
```

Priya Nair: Thanks — I remember a similar shadow in the allocator when we switched kernel selection heuristics (Nov kernel switch). The allocator introduced a small per-request scratch allocation that we didn't roll into the batching estimator. Might be the same class of bug.

Jonah Kim: FWIW I ran the per-sequence microbench yesterday. Kernel change improved throughput but added ~120 bytes/seq of ephemeral metadata for KV bookkeeping on certain kernels. With 4k concurrent in-flight sequences that becomes significant.

Lena Ortiz: Pushed a quick instrument to trace per-seq overhead in estimator: `estimator:per_seq_overhead_bytes` in traces. Early numbers: median=128, p90=256, p99=640 for the short-seq workload. That matches the extra ~250MB we were missing.

Mark Patel: Can we just add a safety margin to the estimator? e.g., +10% or add a fixed per-seq delta? Concern is cost impact (throughput / packing efficiency).

Alex Cohen: Proposal: extend estimator to compute total = base_batch_bytes + per_seq_overhead * batch_size + kv_cache_reserved + workspace_safety. Then choose conservative bin when growth rate > X. Two levers: (1) dynamic per_seq_overhead sampled from recent traces, (2) fallback cap on predicted slots growth per-second.

Priya Nair: I like dynamic sampling. Implementation sketch: maintain EWMA of per_seq_overhead by model+kernel combo (window 5k requests). Use EWMA in estimator, with floor at 128 bytes for safety. Add an opt-in feature flag `batch_reconciler.strict` to enable in prod after smoke.

Jonah Kim: I ran a simulation with the EWMA approach on last week's traffic trace: OOMs -> 0, pad-waste up ~2% at worst, median token latency unchanged. I'll post numbers in the GH comment.

Lena Ortiz: Minimal code diff attached for quick review: 
```
# diff (pseudocode)
- predicted = max_seq * per_seq_base
+ predicted = max_seq * (per_seq_base + ewma_per_seq_overhead[model,kernel])
+ predicted += workspace_margin_bytes
```

Lena Ortiz: Also added an exponential backoff on batch growth when estimator variance spikes. That prevents runaway bin growth from transient spikes.

Mark Patel: What's the perf hit? Sim reported 2% extra memory usage (packing worse) but cleared OOM risk. Are we comfortable shipping that as default?

Alex Cohen: Recommend feature-flag roll-out: enable on dedicated pools first, monitor `oom_count`, `pad_waste`, `batch_growth_rate`. If green for 48h, flip for hosted.

infra-bot: deploy started: canary=redwood-dedicated-canary-03, diff: batch-estimator-ewma + safety margins (rollback on oom spike > 1/min).

Priya Nair: I'll prepare a short eval dashboard: per_seq_overhead EWMA, batch_growth_rate, resident_vs_predicted ratio. Want to catch regressions where overhead jumps (e.g., new kernel variants).

Jonah Kim: Also add a guard for KV shadowing when using buffer reuse: sometimes reuse reduces observed resident but leaves stale header accounting; estimator should track resident delta rather than just allocation intent.

Lena Ortiz: Adding a tiny unit test + trace-based sim. Will open PR with both the estimator change and a benchmark harness.

Alex Cohen: Nice. Action items: Priya — dashboard & flag rollout plan. Lena — PR + tests. Jonah — sims + perf notes about kernel bookkeeping. I'll coordinate canary monitoring.

Mark Patel: Thx team. If sims hold, prioritize the canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:

Alex Cohen: Also capturing this for postmortem notes: root cause = missing per-sequence metadata accounting after kernel switch + aggressive batch growth heuristic. We'll surface in the runtime perf retrospective.
